title: Bibcode (identifier)
summary: The bibcode is a fixed-length 19-character identifier used by astronomical data systems to uniquely reference literature. It encodes the publication year, venue, volume, section, page range, and first author's surname initial. Periods pad shorter fields, and modern usage increasingly allows non-numeric page data, rendering the code's semantic structure unreliable over time.

mechanisms.title: Structural encoding of bibliographic fields
mechanisms.explanation: The 19-character string positions year, venue code, volume, section marker, page numbers, and author surname initial. Periods serve as padding for unused or short fields, with right-padding for publication code and left-padding for volume/page fields.

mechanisms.title: Adaptation for modern identifier formats
mechanisms.explanation: Physical Review article IDs since the late 1990s are mapped by converting the issue number's first two digits to a lowercase letter placed in the section column, while the remaining four digits occupy the page field. The code no longer guarantees numeric page values due to electronic identifier shifts.
